shorts.title: Robert Smalls Stole a Confederate Ship and Sailed His Family to Freedom
shorts.description: In 1862, Robert Smalls used his knowledge of Charleston Harbor to escape slavery aboard the Confederate steamer Planter—and deliver intelligence to the Union.

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: Before dawn at the docks
scenes.script: At about three in the morning on May 13, 1862, Robert Smalls took control of the Confederate steamer Planter in Charleston Harbor. The white officers had gone ashore.
scenes.caption: HE STOLE A CONFEDERATE SHIP

scenes.name: Families board
scenes.script: Smalls and the Black crew picked up their families, raised Confederate and South Carolina flags, and headed into the harbor as if nothing were wrong.
scenes.caption: Crew + families board the Planter

scenes.name: Past Fort Sumter
scenes.script: Smalls knew the harbor signals. He even used the captain's straw hat to help sell the disguise as the ship passed Fort Sumter.
scenes.caption: Charleston → Fort Sumter → Union blockade

scenes.name: Freedom and intelligence
scenes.script: Beyond the fort, the crew lowered the Confederate flags, raised a white sheet, and sailed to the Union blockade. Smalls escaped slavery and delivered the ship and military intelligence.
scenes.caption: FROM ENSLAVED PILOT → WAR HERO

shorts.title: Daniel Morgan Told His Soldiers to Retreat on Purpose
shorts.description: At Cowpens in 1781, Daniel Morgan turned a planned withdrawal into one of the American Revolution's smartest battlefield traps.
researchNotes: National Park Service — Daniel Morgan and Cowpens

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: Morgan's risky plan
scenes.script: At Cowpens in 1781, Daniel Morgan knew Patriot militia could break when British troops charged. So he built a controlled withdrawal into his plan.
scenes.caption: HE ORDERED HIS MEN TO RETREAT

scenes.name: Three American lines
scenes.script: His sharpshooters would fire and fall back. The militia behind them were ordered to fire two volleys, then withdraw behind the Continental regulars.
scenes.caption: SHOOT TWICE → FALL BACK

scenes.name: The British rush in
scenes.script: British troops charged forward, thinking the Americans were collapsing. Instead, they ran into a solid Continental line that held.
scenes.caption: The trap closes

scenes.name: The counterattack
scenes.script: Then American cavalry and returning militia struck from the sides and rear. Morgan had turned an apparent retreat into a famous tactical victory.
scenes.caption: A controlled withdrawal becomes victory

shorts.title: Boston Was Hit by a Flood of Molasses
shorts.description: The Great Molasses Flood of 1919 turned Boston's North End into a deadly river after a huge storage tank burst.
researchNotes: Boston Public Library — Boston's Great Molasses Flood

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: A tank over the neighborhood
scenes.script: Shortly after noon on January 15, 1919, a huge storage tank burst in Boston's North End. It held more than 2.3 million gallons of molasses.
scenes.caption: BOSTON WAS HIT BY A MOLASSES WAVE

scenes.name: The wave
scenes.script: A dark wave reported as high as about fifteen feet rushed through nearby streets at roughly thirty-five miles per hour.
scenes.caption: A DEADLY MOLASSES WAVE

scenes.name: The damage
scenes.script: Buildings were smashed. People and horses were trapped. Twenty-one people died, and around one hundred fifty were injured.
scenes.caption: 21 DEAD · ABOUT 150 INJURED

scenes.name: Aftermath
scenes.script: Cleanup took weeks. Investigators blamed structural weakness in the tank, and the disaster helped push stronger construction standards.
scenes.caption: A strange disaster with real consequences

shorts.title: A 14-Year-Old Got the Idea for Electronic Television While Plowing
shorts.description: Philo Farnsworth's farm-field idea became an early foundation of fully electronic television.

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: Rows in an Idaho field
scenes.script: In 1921, fourteen-year-old Philo Farnsworth was plowing a field in Idaho when its straight rows gave him an idea.
scenes.caption: TELEVISION STARTED WITH FARM ROWS?

scenes.name: Break a picture into lines
scenes.script: What if a picture could be broken into lines, transmitted electronically, then rebuilt on a screen? Existing experiments often used mechanical scanning.
scenes.caption: Could an image travel line by line?

scenes.name: The electronic lab
scenes.script: Farnsworth wanted a fully electronic system. In 1927, his San Francisco team transmitted a simple electronic image using an image dissector.
scenes.caption: 1927 · A FULLY ELECTRONIC IMAGE

scenes.name: A field becomes a screen
scenes.script: He was only twenty-one. An idea inspired by furrows in a farm field became one of the foundations of electronic television.
scenes.caption: THE FARM-ROW IDEA CHANGED TELEVISION

shorts.title: The Enslaved Spy Who Fooled the British at Yorktown
shorts.description: James Armistead Lafayette secretly gathered intelligence in British lines during the campaign that ended at Yorktown.

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: A secret mission
scenes.script: In 1781, an enslaved Virginian named James Armistead began working for the Marquis de Lafayette during the American Revolution.
scenes.caption: THE BRITISH TRUSTED THEIR OWN SPY

scenes.name: Inside British lines
scenes.script: James entered British lines pretending to be a runaway seeking work. He gained the confidence of senior British officers.
scenes.caption: He made the British trust him

scenes.name: Information moves
scenes.script: He carried information on troop movements, supplies, and strategy back to Lafayette while giving misleading information to the British.
scenes.caption: BRITISH CAMP → LAFAYETTE

scenes.name: Freedom delayed
scenes.script: His intelligence helped commanders understand Cornwallis's movements at Yorktown. After helping win a war about liberty, James still had to fight for his own freedom. He was emancipated in 1787.
scenes.caption: EMANCIPATED · 1787

shorts.title: The Woman Who Served in Washington's Army as Robert Shurtleff
shorts.description: Deborah Sampson enlisted in the Continental Army disguised as a man and received an honorable discharge in 1783.
researchNotes: National Women's History Museum — Deborah Sampson

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: Robert Shurtleff enlists
scenes.script: In 1782, Deborah Sampson disguised herself as a man, used the name Robert Shurtleff, and joined the Fourth Massachusetts Regiment.
scenes.caption: THE ARMY THOUGHT SHE WAS A MAN

scenes.name: Light infantry work
scenes.script: She served in light infantry and carried out dangerous scouting work around New York during the final years of the Revolution.
scenes.caption: SCOUTING AROUND NEW YORK

scenes.name: A dangerous secret
scenes.script: After being wounded, she reportedly removed a musket ball herself rather than risk being exposed. The documented service is already extraordinary without adding disputed battles.
scenes.caption: HER IDENTITY STAYED HIDDEN

scenes.name: An honorable discharge
scenes.script: Her identity was discovered after she became seriously ill in Philadelphia. Deborah Sampson received an honorable discharge in October 1783.
scenes.caption: HONORABLY DISCHARGED · 1783

shorts.title: Garrett Morgan Added the Missing Pause Between Stop and Go
shorts.description: Garrett Morgan's three-position traffic signal created a safer all-stop phase for crowded streets.
researchNotes: National Inventors Hall of Fame — Garrett Morgan

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: Crowded Cleveland streets
scenes.script: By the early 1920s, crowded streets had cars, trolleys, horses, and pedestrians fighting for the same intersections.
scenes.caption: STOP. GO. SOMETHING WAS MISSING.

scenes.name: A dangerous collision
scenes.script: After seeing a serious collision in Cleveland, inventor Garrett Morgan designed a better way to control the crossing.
scenes.caption: ONE COLLISION INSPIRES A FIX

scenes.name: The all-stop phase
scenes.script: His three-position signal created a phase where traffic in all directions stopped before another direction was allowed to move.
scenes.caption: ALL DIRECTIONS STOP

scenes.name: A safer interval
scenes.script: Morgan patented it in 1923. It was not exactly today's yellow light, but it tackled the same problem: a safe pause between conflicting movements.
scenes.caption: PATENTED · 1923

shorts.title: Josephine Cochrane Built the Practical Dishwasher Because Hand-Washing Damaged Her Dishes
shorts.description: Josephine Garis Cochran designed a practical dishwasher with wire racks and pressurized hot water in the 1880s.
researchNotes: National Inventors Hall of Fame — Josephine Garis Cochran

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: Chipped dishware
scenes.script: In the 1880s, Josephine Garis Cochran was frustrated that hand-washing frequently chipped her dishware. So she decided to build a better machine.
scenes.caption: SHE BUILT A MACHINE TO SAVE HER DISHES

scenes.name: The working mechanism
scenes.script: Working with mechanic George Butters, she made a system that held dishes in wire compartments while pressurized hot soapy water cleaned them.
scenes.caption: WIRE RACKS + PRESSURIZED WATER

scenes.name: Patent and fair
scenes.script: Her patent was granted in 1886, and her dishwasher gained attention at Chicago's 1893 World's Columbian Exposition.
scenes.caption: PATENT · 1886

scenes.name: From institutions to homes
scenes.script: Hotels and restaurants adopted it before ordinary homes did, because early households often could not supply enough hot water. Her company later became part of KitchenAid.
scenes.caption: A PRACTICAL KITCHEN MACHINE

shorts.title: Bass Reeves Was a Real-Life Frontier Lawman Before Hollywood Cowboys
shorts.description: Deputy U.S. Marshal Bass Reeves spent decades pursuing fugitives across Indian Territory before Oklahoma statehood.

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: From enslavement to freedom
scenes.script: Bass Reeves was born enslaved in the 1830s. After the Civil War he became free, and in 1875 he was hired as a deputy U.S. marshal out of Fort Smith.
scenes.caption: BORN ENSLAVED → FRONTIER LAWMAN

scenes.name: A huge territory
scenes.script: His territory included the enormous and dangerous Indian Territory, much of modern Oklahoma. It demanded long travel, tracking, and careful planning.
scenes.caption: FORT SMITH → INDIAN TERRITORY

scenes.name: Thirty-two years
scenes.script: Historical accounts describe Reeves using disguises and tracking skills to make arrests. He spent thirty-two years pursuing fugitives.
scenes.caption: DISGUISES · TRACKING · ARRESTS

scenes.name: The West came after him
scenes.script: He stayed in federal service until Oklahoma became a state in 1907, then briefly served as a Muskogee police officer. The lawman came before the Hollywood legend.
scenes.caption: THE LAWMAN CAME FIRST

shorts.title: John Paul Jones Won a Naval Battle—Then His Own Ship Sank
shorts.description: John Paul Jones captured HMS Serapis in 1779, but his battered Bonhomme Richard sank two days later.
researchNotes: Naval History and Heritage Command — John Paul Jones

history.message: Added from the American Stories Batch 2 preset.

scenes.name: Off the English coast
scenes.script: On September 23, 1779, John Paul Jones fought the British warship Serapis off Flamborough Head aboard Bonhomme Richard.
scenes.caption: HE WON—THEN HIS SHIP SANK

scenes.name: A battered ship
scenes.script: The British ship was stronger. Jones's vessel was blasted apart, burning, and taking on water—but he did not surrender.
scenes.caption: BONHOMME RICHARD IS BREAKING APART

scenes.name: Point-blank battle
scenes.script: Jones forced the two ships together, turning the fight into a brutal point-blank battle. After hours of combat, Serapis surrendered.
scenes.caption: HE CAPTURED THE ENEMY SHIP

scenes.name: The final twist
scenes.script: But Bonhomme Richard was too damaged to save. It sank two days later, so Jones sailed away aboard the British ship he had just captured.
scenes.caption: HE WON—THEN HIS SHIP SANK
